slot.brief: Concave mirror where the object and image have a stated relation (e.g., image distance equals some multiple of object distance or magnification given); use mirror formula plus magnification to solve for focal length.

stem: A concave mirror forms a real image with magnification $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ when an object is placed $24\ \text{cm}$ in front of it. What is the mirror’s focal length?

verdicts.working: Using the mirror sign convention, u = -24 cm. From m = -v/u = -1/2, v = -12 cm. Thus 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = -1/8 cm⁻¹, so the focal length magnitude is 8 cm.

working:
$u=-24\ \text{cm},\quad m=-\dfrac vu=-\dfrac12\Rightarrow v=-12\ \text{cm}$; $\dfrac1f=\dfrac1v+\dfrac1u=-\dfrac1{12}-\dfrac1{24}=-\dfrac18\ \text{cm}^{-1}$; $|f|=8\ \text{cm}$.

Independent check: Using the mirror sign convention, u = -24 cm. From m = -v/u = -1/2, v = -12 cm. Thus 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = -1/8 cm⁻¹, so the focal length magnitude is 8 cm.
solution:
Using $m=-v/u$, with $u=-24\ \text{cm}$, we get $v=-12\ \text{cm}$.
$$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}=-\frac{1}{12}-\frac{1}{24}=-\frac{1}{8}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$$
Hence the focal length has magnitude $8\ \text{cm}$.
